<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par132" />{{GHGmargin-letter|132|b}}
Rem. 1. Where an adjectival attribute appears to stand ''before'' its substantive (according to the usual explanation, for the sake of special emphasis) the relation is really appositional in character; thus, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=30}} {{GHGheb|text=עֲנִיָּה עֲנָתוֹת|translate=O thou poor one, Anathoth!}} (but probably {{GHGheb|text=עֲנִ֫יהָ|translate=answer her}}, is to be read); cf. 23:12, 53:11 (''a righteous man, my servant''; but in 28:21 {{GHGheb|text=זָר}} and {{GHGheb|text=נָכְרִי}} are {{GHGterm|predicates}} preceding the substantives); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=6}}, 10 f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=4}} ''him who is worthy to be praised will I call upon'', ''the Lord''; 92:12 (apposition after participles).—But {{GHGheb|text=רַבִּים}} and {{GHGheb|text=רַבּוֹת|translate=many}}, are sometimes placed, like numerals, before the substantive, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=16|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=28}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=145|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=רַב}} is a ''subst. regens'', in 89:51 the text is corrupt); an appositional relation can scarcely be intended in these instances.

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|c}}
2. In a few expressions (mostly poetic) the adjective appears not as an attribute ''after'' the substantive, but in the construct state governing it; so in the singular, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=15|verse=16}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=גֹּדֶל}} should be read); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=16|verse=7}} (''the height of his stature''); in the plural, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=40}} {{GHGheb|text=חַלֻּקֵי אֲבָנִים|translate=smooth ones of}} (among) ''stones'', i.e. ''smooth stones''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=35|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=46|verse=5}}, and with a following collective instead of a plural, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=29|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶבְיוֹנֵי אָדָם|translate=the poor among men}}, i.e. ''poor men''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=11|verse=7}}; cf. in Latin ''canum degeneres''. However, in almost all these cases the adjective which is made into a ''regens'' is strongly emphatic, and is frequently equivalent to a superlative (see below, {{GHGpar|133|g}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|d}}
3. When ''two'' adjectives follow a feminine, sometimes only that standing next to the noun takes the feminine termination, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=19|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=רוּחַ גְּדֹלָה וְחָזָק וגו׳}} (but read {{GHGheb|text=גָּדוֹל}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=9}} (but cf. {{GHGpar|75|y}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=20|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=63|verse=2}}. A similar dislike of the feminine form may also be observed in the case of verbal predicates referring to feminine subjects, cf. {{GHGpar|145|p}} and ''t''.

When an attribute qualifies several substantives of different genders, it agrees with the masculine, as being the ''prior gender'' (cf. {{GHGpar|146|d}}), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=9|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=חֻקִּים וּמִצְוֹת טוֹבִים}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=34|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=8|verse=5}}.

When ''three'' attributes follow a substantive, the first two may stand without a conjunction, and the last be attached by {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=1|verse=8}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|e}}
4. After feminines plural ending in {{GHGheb|text=־ִים}} ({{GHGpar|87|p}}) the adjectival attribute (in accordance with the fundamental rule stated above, under ''a'') takes the ending {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=בֵּיצִים עֲזֻבוֹת|translate=forsaken eggs}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=16}}. For a strange exception see {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=29|verse=17}} (differently in 24:2).

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|f}}
5. With regard to ''number'' it is to be remarked that—

(''a'') Substantives in the ''dual'' are followed by adjectives (or participles) in the ''plural'', e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=28}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=6|verse=17}}) {{GHGheb|text=עֵינַ֫יִם רָמוֹת|translate=haughty eyes}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=35|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=3}} f., cf. {{GHGpar|88|a}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|g}}
(''b'') ''Collective'' ideas are not infrequently joined with the ''plural'' of the adjective or participle (''constructio ad sensum''); thus, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צֹאן|translate=sheep}} [with ''fem. plur.''], {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=43}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=עַם}}=''men'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=13|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=9|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל}}=''all the Israelites'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=גָּלוּת}}=''the exiles'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=4}}; cf. also {{GHGheb|text=נֶ֫פֶשׁ שְׁנָ֫יִם|translate=two souls}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=46|verse=27}}.<ref>But it is impossible to take {{GHGheb|text=תְּמִימִם}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=6}} as an attribute of {{GHGheb|text=בָּקָר}}; probably it is a correction intended to harmonize the passage with {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=28|verse=11}} where ''two'' young bullocks are required.</ref> Cf. similar phenomena in the connexion of collectives with plural predicates in {{GHGpar|145|c}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|132|h}}
(''c'') The ''pluralis excellentiae'' or ''pluralis maiestatis'' is joined, as a rule, to the singular of the attribute, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים צַדִּיק}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=19|verse=4}}, 16 (={{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=4}}, 17); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=19|verse=4}}; but cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים חַיִּים}}<ref>Cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=13}}, where {{GHGheb|text=אֱלֹהִים}} (in the sense of ''a spirit'') is followed by {{GHGheb|text=עֹלִים}} as a second accusative; conversely in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=13}}, 16, a singular suffix refers back to {{GHGheb|text=תְּרָפִים|translate=household god}} (but not so in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=31|verse=34}}), as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=46|verse=4}} to the plural of amplification {{GHGheb|text=יַמִּים|translate=sea}}. On the other hand, it is very doubtful whether {{GHGheb|text=רַבָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=15}} is to be regarded as an attribute of {{GHGheb|text=תְּהֹמוֹת}} and not rather as the adverb, ''abundantly''.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=26}}, 36, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=23|verse=36|hidebook=1}}, perhaps also<section end="par132" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
